name: Simon
overview: Simon was a male man from Cyrene who is noted in Scripture for carrying the cross of the Messiah during the crucifixion. No tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded about him. His role is unique and significant in the Passion narrative as the one who bore the cross for Jesus.
namesAndTitles: The name Simon is a proper name meaning 'he has heard' or 'obedient one.' This name, while common, reflects a character of responsiveness or submission, fitting for one who obeyed the call to carry Christ's cross as recorded in Matthew 27:32.
familyAndRelationships: Simon is identified as the son of Alexander and Rufus according to Mark 15:21. These explicit familial relationships provide a brief glimpse into his personal background, though Scripture does not elaborate further on his family.
scriptureSignificance: Simon of Cyrene holds an important place in the biblical account of Jesus' crucifixion by assisting in carrying the cross, an act that symbolizes bearing Christ's burden. His involvement highlights the human participation in the Passion and serves as a reminder of the call to discipleship through sharing in Christ's suffering. This act is recorded in Matthew 27:32 and Mark 15:21, underscoring his role in the fulfillment of the Passion narrative.
